name: ADHD Clinic — Milestone 2 v2: Google Calendar Booking System (No Third-Party Platform)

_notes.overview: This workflow handles the full appointment booking lifecycle using ONLY Gmail + Google Calendar. When a patient emails requesting an appointment, the system detects it, checks consultant availability, proposes a slot, and once confirmed books it directly into Google Calendar with a confirmation email sent to the patient.
_notes.architecture: Google Calendar is the single source of truth. Consultants manage availability by creating 'Available' events in their calendar. The system reads these, proposes them to patients, and converts them to confirmed appointments when the patient replies to confirm.
_notes.flow: Patient emails → detected as booking request → system reads next available slot from Google Calendar → replies with proposed time → patient confirms → appointment created in Google Calendar → confirmation email sent → slot marked as booked
_notes.twoPhaseBooking: Phase 1 (auto): System detects booking request, proposes next available slot. Phase 2 (auto): System detects confirmation reply, finalises the booking in Google Calendar.

nodes.name: 📬 Gmail — Watch New Emails
nodes.notes:
Same Gmail trigger as Milestone 1.
Polls every 60 seconds for new unread emails.
Handles BOTH: general enquiries (routed to Milestone 1 logic) AND booking requests (handled here).
Unread only — prevents duplicate processing.

nodes.name: 🔧 Normalize Email Data
nodes.notes:
Extracts and normalizes all fields from the Gmail payload.
Also detects whether this is a fresh email or a reply to our slot proposal.
This is important — replies from patients confirming an appointment are handled differently to new enquiries.

nodes.name: 🚨 Safety Filter
nodes.notes:
Identical safety filter from Milestone 1.
Checks for: legal/complaint, safeguarding, and crisis language.
If flagged → admin alert, NO auto-reply, NO booking attempted.
This runs on ALL emails before any logic.

nodes.name: ⚡ Is Safety Flagged?
nodes.notes:
Hard gate.
True (flagged) → admin alert, stop.
False (clean) → AI intent detection.

values.content: You are an intent classifier for an ADHD clinic. Analyse the email and return ONLY valid JSON. No markdown. No explanation.

=Classify this email intent.

Subject: {{ $json.subject }}
Body: {{ $json.body }}
Is Reply: {{ $json.isReply }}

Return JSON:
{
  "intent": one of ["booking_request", "booking_confirmation", "booking_cancellation", "general_enquiry", "follow_up", "manual_review"],
  "confidence": 0.0 to 1.0,
  "appointmentType": "what type of appointment they want in plain English, or empty string",
  "firstName": "patient first name if mentioned, else empty string",
  "isChild": true or false,
  "preferredDate": "any date or time preference mentioned, else empty string",
  "reasoning": "one sentence"
}

Rules:
- booking_request: patient wants to book a new appointment
- booking_confirmation: patient is replying YES to a slot we proposed
- booking_cancellation: patient wants to cancel an existing appointment
- general_enquiry: question, information request, not a booking
- follow_up: existing patient following up on their care
- manual_review: anything ambiguous or confidence below 0.75
- If isReply=true and body contains yes/confirm/that works/perfect/sounds good → booking_confirmation

nodes.name: 🤖 AI — Detect Intent
nodes.notes:
Classifies the EMAIL INTENT — is this a booking request, a confirmation reply, a cancellation, or a general enquiry?

This is the key decision node that separates:
- Booking requests → find available slot → propose it
- Confirmation replies → finalise the booking in Google Calendar
- Cancellations → remove from Google Calendar
- General enquiries → pass to Milestone 1 email triage logic

Temperature 0.1 = highly consistent output.
Confidence < 0.75 → manual review.

nodes.name: 🧩 Parse AI Intent
nodes.notes:
Parses and validates the AI intent response.
Same bulletproof approach as Milestone 1:
- Strips markdown fences
- Catches JSON parse errors
- Enforces confidence threshold
- Every failure mode → manual_review

nodes.name: 🔀 Route by Intent
nodes.notes:
Routes emails by detected intent:
- booking_request → find available slots → propose to patient
- booking_confirmation → create confirmed calendar event
- booking_cancellation → remove from calendar, notify consultant
- general_enquiry → handle with standard email templates (Milestone 1 logic)
- follow_up → handle with follow-up template
- fallback (manual_review) → alert admin

nodes.name: 📅 Prepare Availability Search
nodes.notes:
Prepares the date range for searching available slots.
Default: today → 14 days ahead.
If the patient mentioned a preferred date (e.g. 'next Tuesday'), the search starts from that date.
Outputs calendarSearchFrom and calendarSearchTo for the Google Calendar query.

nodes.name: 📅 Get Available Slots from Calendar
nodes.notes:
Queries Google Calendar for events with 'Available' in the title within the next 14 days.

REPLACE:
- calendarId: consultant's calendar ID
  (Google Calendar → Settings → Calendar name → Calendar ID)

CONVENTION: Consultants mark open slots in Google Calendar as:
  'Available 10:00-11:00' or 'Available'
The query searches for this keyword.

For multiple consultants: add a consultant selection step before this node
based on appointment type (e.g. child ADHD → paediatric consultant's calendar).

Returns up to 20 events, ordered by start time — we'll filter to 3 best options next.

nodes.name: 🗓️ Select Slots & Build Proposal
nodes.notes:
Picks the best 3 available slots from the calendar results.
Formats them in a friendly, readable UK date format:
  'Option 1: Monday, 24 February 2026 at 10:00–11:00'

Builds a natural, non-robotic proposal email with all 3 options.
Patient just replies with their preferred option.

Also stores slot IDs and times so we can book the correct one when the patient confirms.

If NO slots are available → noSlotsFound = true → routes to manual handling node.

nodes.name: ⚡ Any Slots Available?
nodes.notes:
If no available slots found in the next 14 days:
→ Alert admin to handle manually (avoid sending a blank or confusing email)

If slots found:
→ Send the proposal email to the patient

nodes.notes:
Alerts admin when no available slots are found in the calendar.
Includes full patient details and their original message so admin can respond promptly.
Admin should: add availability to Google Calendar, then reply to patient manually.

nodes.name: 📤 Send Slot Proposal to Patient
nodes.notes:
Sends the 3-option slot proposal to the patient.
Replies within the same Gmail thread (threadId) so it stays organised.
Patient just hits reply and says which option they want.

REPLACE:
- replyTo: your clinic email
- sendAsEmail: your clinic email

nodes.name: 📊 Log Booking Request to Sheet
nodes.notes:
Logs the booking request with status SLOTS_PROPOSED.
Stores all 3 proposed slot times so admin can see what was offered.
Stores the threadId so the confirmation reply can be matched to this record.

Sheet tab: 'Bookings'
Required columns:
Timestamp | Patient Name | Patient Email | Appointment Type | Preferred Date | Status | Slot 1 | Slot 2 | Slot 3 | Thread ID | Calendar Event ID | Notes

nodes.name: 🔍 Detect Chosen Slot
nodes.notes:
Analyses the patient's confirmation reply to determine which slot they chose.

Detects:
- Explicit: 'Option 1', 'second option', '3rd option'
- Implicit: 'yes', 'that works', 'sounds good', 'perfect' → defaults to Option 1
- Ambiguous: 'the Monday one' → routes to admin for manual confirmation

If the patient's choice is unclear → needsManualReview = true → admin handles it.
This prevents booking the wrong slot.

nodes.name: ⚡ Slot Choice Clear?
nodes.notes:
If slot choice is ambiguous → admin alert (no accidental wrong booking).
If choice is clear → proceed to create the Google Calendar event.

nodes.name: 🟡 Alert Admin — Unclear Choice
nodes.notes:
Alerts admin when the patient's confirmation reply is ambiguous.
Includes the patient's full reply so admin can read it and book the correct slot.
Prevents the system from ever booking the wrong appointment.

nodes.name: 📋 Prepare Confirmed Booking
nodes.notes:
Prepares the confirmed booking data for Google Calendar.
Maps the patient's chosen option number to the correct slot start/end times.
Builds the calendar event title: 'ADHD Assessment — Patient Name'

For a more robust setup: add a Google Sheets lookup node before this one
that searches the Bookings sheet by threadId to retrieve the original slot times.
This handles cases where the confirmation comes in a new conversation context.

nodes.name: 📅 Create Confirmed Appointment
nodes.notes:
Creates the confirmed appointment in Google Calendar.

Event includes:
- Title: Appointment Type — Patient Name
- Description: all patient contact details
- Location: clinic address or Zoom link
- Attendee: patient (receives Google Calendar invite)
- Reminders: 24hr email + 1hr popup + 30min popup
- Status: confirmed
- Visibility: private (GDPR)

The 'Available' event for this slot should be deleted separately
(or renamed to 'Booked') — see next node.

nodes.name: 🗑️ Remove Available Slot (Now Booked)
nodes.notes:
Deletes the 'Available' slot event from Google Calendar now that it's been booked.
This prevents other patients from being offered the same slot.

IMPORTANT: This is what prevents double booking.
The slot disappears from the calendar the moment it's confirmed.
